basis: Primordial dwarfism, microcephaly/neuropathy and endocrine dysfunction define syndrome; cardiomyopathy in 1/2 reported patients; individual renal anomalies each 1/5.
Usually infectious inflammation of epididymis; reproductive site has no axis. Associated urinary infection is a separate disease.
Paralysis of pupillary and accommodation function, classified under oculomotor nerve paralysis and ocular disorders.
Inherited histidine/folate metabolic defect; anemia and developmental impairment are occasional (5-29%), despite historical severe-family descriptions.
Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; hepatic steatosis/injury, ventricular hypertrophy/heart failure and brain atrophy each reported in 1/1 phenotyped patients.
Nontuberculous mycobacterial infection; destructive pulmonary infection accounts for the great majority of clinical disease (>80%).
Carcinoma originates in bronchial squamous epithelium; metastatic sites are not defining organ involvement.
Chronic developmental lung and airway injury; right-heart findings relate to separately diagnosed pulmonary hypertension/cor pulmonale.
Juvenile iron overload with hepatic injury and endocrine dysfunction; direct iron cardiomyopathy in about 30% (2/7 reported), near threshold.
Branched-chain amino-acid metabolic defect; intermediate-like phenotype commonly causes developmental impairment and metabolic encephalopathy (>30%).
Incomplete closure of a cardiac valve; pulmonary valve belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
Inherited phosphate disorder; tendon calcification, osteosclerosis and osteopenia reported in 1/1 patients. Cerebral calcification alone does not establish functional damage.
Myopathy, Paget bone disease and frontotemporal degeneration define syndrome; cardiac disease and respiratory muscle weakness are occasional (5-29%).
Inherited progressive encephalopathy with brain edema and white-matter degeneration; no additional common organ damage established across subtypes.
Inherited severe skin fragility; oral mucosal blistering reported in 1/1 and enamel hypoplasia frequent (30-79%). Laryngeal structural disease is occasional.
Developmental impairment, brain malformations and seizures define disorder; vertebral anomalies occur in 4/15 (~27%), below threshold.
HCN1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; seizures and intellectual disability are defining.
Localized keratotic epithelial lesions of glans/preputial skin; infection is a risk factor rather than the defining mechanism.
Perivascular glomus-cell neoplasm originating from modified vascular smooth-muscle cells, usually in dermis or subcutis.
Duane ocular motility abnormality and radial-ray skeletal malformations define Okihiro syndrome; additional common organ damage is not established here.
Ischemic myocardial injury involving the subendocardial heart wall.
Defined by pestivirus infection; supplied information establishes no consistent organ-specific damage.
Isolated sperm structural and motility defects causing male infertility; no endocrine or other axis involvement established.
Hereditary arthritis of the sacroiliac joints; an autoimmune or infectious mechanism is not established by the supplied record.
Rickettsial infection; transient rash does not qualify as skin damage, and lasting organ complications are not common enough for additional labels.
